chapter.title: Memory: the intern forgets everything overnight

cards.body:
The model inside every AI agent has total amnesia. It forgets you the moment it finishes a reply.

Our intern is the same. They walk in each morning with no memory of yesterday, so you hand them a folder of everything so far. **That folder is the only memory they have.**
cards.simpler:
The model inside every AI agent forgets everything. It forgets you as soon as it finishes a reply.

Our intern is the same. They walk in each morning with no memory of yesterday. So each day you hand them a folder with everything that has happened so far. **That folder is the only memory they have.**

cards.prompt: Your trip-planning agent is on step 12. Before the model picks step 13, how does it know what happened in steps 1 to 11?

options.text: It remembers them, the way you remember breakfast.
The agent hands it a written record of steps 1 to 11 again.
It doesn't need to. Each step is picked fresh, with no past.

whyNot.a: That's how people work, not models: the model keeps nothing between replies.
whyNot.c: That's the amnesia without the fix: with no record, it would start from step 1 every time.

cards.reteach: The model works like a calculator: once the answer is out, it keeps nothing. So the agent program keeps the record and puts the whole thing back in front of the model every turn. No folder, no memory.

cards.title: How the faking works
cards.body:
A model is *stateless*, which means each call starts blank, like a calculator after you press clear. It doesn't keep your chat anywhere.

So the agent program does the remembering. Each turn it bundles up the goal, every step so far and every tool result, and sends **the whole conversation again, from the top**. The model reads it, picks the next step, and forgets.

You'd think the model remembers the chat. It's the other way round. It's like an actor who gets handed the entire script before every single line.
cards.simpler:
A model is stateless. That means each call starts blank, like a calculator after you press clear. It doesn't keep your chat anywhere.

So the agent program does the remembering. Each turn it gathers the goal, every step so far and every tool result. Then it sends **the whole conversation again, from the top**. The model reads it, picks the next step, and forgets.

It's like an actor handed the full script before every line.

cards.title: The oat milk survey
cards.body: An agent is told to check 50 café suppliers for the price of oat milk and to email any that don't list it online. For 30 steps it's sharp: visit the site, note the price, move on. Around step 40 the record gets too long, and the agent program cuts the oldest part so the rest fits. That cut takes the note saying *emailed Okafor Bakery* with it. So it emails Okafor Bakery again. And again. The third reply just says: "Yes. Still $1.80."
cards.simpler: An agent must check 50 café suppliers for the price of oat milk. It must also email any supplier that doesn't show the price online. For 30 steps it does well: visit the site, write down the price, move on. Around step 40 its record gets too long, so **the agent program cuts the oldest part to make room**. The note saying "emailed Okafor Bakery" goes with it. So it emails Okafor Bakery again. And again. The third reply just says: "Yes. Still $1.80."

cards.prompt: Your agent did fine for 10 steps, then at step 40 it books the same hotel again. Most likely cause?

options.text: The model got tired after so many steps.
The step 2 booking was cut from the record so it fits what the model can read at once.
The prompt wasn't firm enough about not repeating steps.

whyNot.a: That's the human picture, not the model: it doesn't get tired, it just reads whatever it's sent.
whyNot.c: That's effort, not memory: no wording brings back a booking it wasn't shown.

cards.reteach: Treat every turn as a brand-new intern reading the folder. If the step 2 booking page was trimmed out to make room, then as far as they know it never happened, so they book again.

cards.title: When the folder outgrows the desk
cards.body:
Here's the catch. A model can only read so much text at once, and that limit is its *context window*. Picture it as the intern's desk: the folder has to fit on it.

Every step makes the folder thicker. Once it won't fit, the agent program has to trim or squeeze the older pages, and the intern redoes work they can't see. A very crowded desk can make them sloppier too. **Long tasks often fail from forgetting, not from stupidity.**

Builders fight this in two ways. They *summarise*, squeezing 30 old steps into one short paragraph. And they keep a *notes file* outside the model: a running checklist the agent writes to and rereads, so "emailed Okafor" survives the cut.
cards.simpler:
A model can only read so much text at once. That limit is its context window. Think of it as the intern's desk: the folder must fit on it.

Every step makes the folder thicker. Once it won't fit, the agent program has to trim old pages, and the intern redoes work they can't see. A very full desk can make them sloppier too. **Long tasks often fail from forgetting, not from stupidity.**

The fix is a short summary of old steps, or a notes file the agent writes to and rereads.

cards.body: Sam's agent starts redoing work at step 40, so Sam adds "DO NOT REPEAT STEPS" to the instructions, in capitals. It repeats them anyway, politely. The model can't avoid repeating something it can't see. To spot this, ask one question: is the record of the earlier step still in what gets sent? If not, **fix the notes, not the wording**.
cards.simpler: Sam's agent starts redoing work at step 40. So Sam adds "DO NOT REPEAT STEPS" to the instructions, in capital letters. The agent repeats them anyway, politely. It can't avoid repeating something it can't see. To catch this, ask one question: is the note about the earlier step still in what gets sent to the model? If not, **fix the notes, not the wording**.

cards.prompt: A friend says: "ChatGPT knew my name in a brand-new chat, so models do remember." What's most likely going on?

options.text: The model learned the name and stored it inside itself.
The app saved a note with the name and sent it along with the new chat.
Its context window got big enough to hold last week.

whyNot.a: That's picturing the model as a brain that files things away: it keeps nothing between calls, so the app did the saving.
whyNot.c: That's desk size, not memory: even a bigger desk starts empty on every call.

cards.reteach: Any memory you see is a note someone saved and handed back. It's like a sticky note on the intern's folder: "Client's name is Ana." They didn't remember it. They read it.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: A model forgets everything the moment it replies, so an agent fakes memory by sending the whole story back every turn. **When the story outgrows what the model can read at once, the agent can start repeating itself**, unless it summarises or keeps notes.
cards.simpler: A model forgets everything the moment it replies. So an agent fakes memory by sending the whole story back every turn. **When the story gets too long for the model to read at once, the agent can start repeating itself.** The way out is a short summary or a notes file.

cards.body:
Tell ChatGPT or Claude your favourite snack. Then open a brand-new chat and ask what your favourite snack is. If it has no idea, that's the amnesia. If it knows, the app saved a note and slipped it in.

Tomorrow: the agent says the file was sent. No tool ever sent it.
cards.simpler:
Tell ChatGPT or Claude your favourite snack. Then open a brand-new chat and ask it what your favourite snack is. If it has no idea, that's the forgetting this chapter is about. If it does know, **the app saved a note and quietly slipped it in** to the new chat.

Tomorrow: the agent says the file was sent. No tool ever sent it.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now explain why an agent that worked fine for 10 steps starts repeating itself at step 40, and name 2 things builders do about it.

dubious_claims: Card 6: 'Once it's bigger than the desk, older pages get cut' is presented as automatic. Usually the model's service rejects text that's too long, and the agent program has to choose to trim or summarise.
Card 6: 'Long tasks fail from forgetting, not from stupidity' overclaims. Models also get worse on very long inputs before they hit the limit.
Card 1: 'Every AI agent has total amnesia' clashes with card 3, which says the agent program does the remembering. Only the model forgets.
Card 8 feedback for option a calls the amnesia a 'myth', which contradicts the chapter and doesn't name the real confusion (thinking the model learns or stores things inside itself).
repairedFrom.why: Exercise 2 asks almost the same thing as exercise 1 (is the old step resent?), and no exercise tests the step-40 repeat problem that the outcome line promises.
repairedFrom.fix: Rewrite card 5: 'Your agent did fine for 10 steps, then at step 40 it books the same hotel again. Most likely cause?' Options: (a) the model got tired, (b) the step-2 booking was cut so the record fits the context window, (c) the prompt wasn't firm enough. Then move 'Tomorrow: the agent says the file was sent…' to be the last line of the try card, so the chapter ends on the open loop.
